title: Secure an SO-101 robot arm to a small table edge with plastic clamps
instruction: Use your left hand to raise and steady the folded SO-101 from its forward rest. Keep both fingers supporting it while your right hand opens and fits each spring clamp directly on a native base foot and under the small table edge. Relax the handles to close each clamp. Withdraw both hands and leave the arm upright and stable.
context: Commissioning an SO-101 workstation includes mounting its complete unpowered arm to the work table. Raising a forward-resting assembly, holding it upright and fitting portable spring clamps tests coordinated support and load transfer into a stable table-edge mount.
setup: A full-size 0.632 kg SO-101 rests folded and tilted forward on three contacts on a fixed 255 × 322 × 16 mm plywood table. Its native base is unclamped. Two nylon spring clamps with elastomer pads start on a nearby 25 mm plywood rail, handles facing the YAM bases. Fit them directly to the two native base feet.
scoring: Score 0.5 per distinct base foot clamped from an open straddle while the left gripper continuously contacts both sides of the folded arm. Upper and lower working pads must contact the base foot and table underside. Retain both hands clear for 2 s within 6 mm X, 8 mm Y, 3 mm height, 3° tilt, 5° yaw and 3 mm drift. A displaced clamp must be fitted again.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz), including the two-second retention interval.
fidelity: Full-scale SO-101 CAD and URDF mass/inertia in a fixed folded joint pose; the complete assembly is free to topple. CAD-derived native-base collision pieces preserve its mounting recess. Free passive spring clamps transfer load through actual pad contacts. Springs, friction and rigid pad compliance are uncalibrated. Native YAM drives and force limits.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 actions, 120 s); demo: 1.0 (944 actions, 47.2 s).
